name: Omnitree Coarsening
definition: Coarsening an internal node reverses the action of refinement, decrementing selected positions from the splitting label and fusing children along one or more dimensions. A request to coarsen the tree consists of a set of fusion markers attached to internal nodes. Definition 3.1: Let v be an internal node of a d-dimensional omnitree with splitting label b(v) and $\sigma(v) = \{j \in D : b_j(v) = 1\}$. A coarsening of v in dimensions $C \subseteq \sigma(v), C \neq \emptyset$, replaces v with a node v' whose splitting label satisfies $b_j(v') = 0$ for $j \in C$ and $b_j(v') = b_j(v)$ for $j \notin C$. The $2^{|\sigma(v)|}$ children of v are fused along each dimension in C, yielding $2^{|\sigma(v) \setminus C|}$ children of v'; in the case that $C = \sigma(v)$, v' is a leaf and as such has no children left.
summary: Omnitree coarsening reverses refinement by fusing last-level child nodes along specified dimensions to reduce tree resolution while preserving leaf boxes.
